title: The Virgin Birth, Twice Told
arabic: قَالَتْ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى وَلَدٌ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِى بَشَرٌ قَالَ كَذَٰلِكِ ٱللَّهُ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ إِذَا قَضَىٰٓ أَمْرًا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
translation: “My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has touched me? God creates what He wills; when He decrees a thing, He says to it: Be, and it is.”

sunni.label: The Qur'an
sunni.body: The virgin birth is a sign of God's power: He need only say “Be,” and it is. Jesus is created by that command, a prophet, not divine.

shia.label: The Gospel
shia.body: The same virgin birth is the Incarnation: the Holy Spirit overshadows Mary, and the child born is God the Son himself, the eternal Word made flesh.

voiceover.hook: In two scriptures, centuries apart, Mary asks the very same question.
voiceover.reference: The Quran, Surah Al Imran, verse forty-seven.
voiceover.question: Christian or Muslim, what does the virgin birth mean to you

cta_text: Christian or Muslim - what does the virgin birth mean to you?
caption_desc: The Quran and the Gospel both say Mary was a virgin. Here is where they meet, and where they part. ✨ #jesus #mary #virginbirth #quran #bible #christianity #islam #interfaith
